Role of KeyM between key master, applications, and CSM

The Key Manager (KeyM) consists of two submodules. The crypto key submodule initializes, updates, and maintains the cryptographic key material of an ECU, for example keys for Secured I-PDUs. These keys are provided by a key master, which can reside in the vehicle or in a backend. Communication with it usually takes place via diagnostic commands (SWS KeyM p. 24). The certificate submodule holds the status of PKI certificates and provides their contents ([SWS_KeyM_00066], [SWS_KeyM_00083]). KeyM does not store key material itself. It passes it to CSM keys via the mandatory interfaces Csm_KeyElementSet, Csm_KeyElementGet, and Csm_KeySetValid ([SWS_KeyM_00076]). Further interfaces used are Csm_KeyDerive, Csm_SignatureVerify, Det_ReportError, and IdsM_SetSecurityEvent ([SWS_KeyM_00078]).

Application SWCs access it via RTE ports. For each certificate there is a port KeyMCertificate_{KeyMCertificate}, for each certificate element a port KeyMCertificateElement_…, plus the ports KeyMCryptoKey and KeyMCryptoKeyNotification ([SWS_KeyM_00160], [SWS_KeyM_00162], [SWS_KeyM_00163], [SWS_KeyM_00164]). BSW modules also use KeyM:

  • The TLS implementation of TcpIp retrieves certificates using KeyM_GetCertificate (SWS TcpIp p. 134).
  • The DCM reads whitelists using KeyM_CertElementGetFirst/KeyM_CertElementGetNext (SWS DCM p. 162).
  • The DCM receives verification results via the Dcm_KeyMAsyncCertificateVerifyFinished configured as a callback (SWS DCM p. 245).

Context diagram: KeyM mediates between applications or DCM/TcpIp and CSM, StbM, NvM, IdsM, and DET; key handlers are configurable extensions. Sources: [SWS_KeyM_00076], [SWS_KeyM_00078], [SWS_KeyM_00160], SWS KeyM (Fig. 9.4) p. 119, SWS TcpIp p. 134

Certificate chain and its configuration

Certificates are described in the configuration via KeyMCertificate containers. At runtime, they are addressed via the handles KeyM_CertificateIdType and KeyM_CertElementIdType, both of type uint16 ([SWS_KeyM_00301], [SWS_KeyM_00300]). Each container contains three references:

  • to the parent certificate; the root certificate references itself here,
  • to a CSM job for signature verification,
  • to a CSM key for the public key of the certificate.

SWS KeyM (Fig. 7.3) p. 22 shows this structure. If all verification steps are error-free, KeyM sets the public key into the CSM key referenced via KeyMCertCsmSignatureVerifyKeyRef and validates it with Csm_KeySetValid ([SWS_KeyM_00170]).

Certificate data is passed as KeyM_CertDataType. The structure consists of certDataLength and a pointer certData to a buffer of the caller ([SWS_KeyM_00041]). The sizes of the RTE data types result from the configuration: KeyMKeyCertNameMaxLength for names and KeyMCertificateElementMaxLength for element buffers ([SWS_KeyM_91000], [SWS_KeyM_91004]).

Context diagram: Three-stage chain Root – Intermediate – Working Certificate with references to one CSM job and one CSM key each; root references itself. Sources: SWS KeyM (Fig. 7.3) p. 22, [SWS_KeyM_00170]

Certificate status: from setting to validity

Each certificate has a status of type KeyM_CertificateStatusType, which KeyM_CertGetStatus provides ([SWS_KeyM_91003], [SWS_KeyM_00066]). The life cycle according to SWS KeyM (Fig. 7.4) p. 24:

  • After KeyM_Init, the certificate is set to KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_AVAILABLE.
  • KeyM_SetCertificate with length > 0, KeyM_ServiceCertificate, or loading during startup leads to the transient status KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_PARSED.
  • After successful parsing, KEYM_CERTIFICATE_PARSED_NOT_VALIDATED follows.
  • KeyM_SetCertificate with length 0 resets the certificate and status.

A certificate reaches KEYM_CERTIFICATE_VALID only after complete, error-free verification ([SWS_KeyM_00170]). If the check fails, a specific error status remains, such as KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_VALIDITY_PERIOD_FAIL, KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_SIGNATURE_FAIL, or KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST ([SWS_KeyM_91003]).

State diagram: A certificate transitions through "not available → not parsed → parsed → valid"; parse and verification errors lead to separate error states. Interpretation: The assignment of verification error states and the reset path from all states are inferred. Sources: SWS KeyM (Fig. 7.4) p. 24, SWS KeyM (Fig. 7.4) p. 33, [SWS_KeyM_91003]

KeyM_SetCertificate stores a presented certificate only temporarily in the configured storage class, typically in RAM. For persistent storage, such as for the root certificate, KeyM_ServiceCertificate is provided ([SWS_KeyM_00057], SWS KeyM p. 31). For asynchronous verification, there are three variants:

  • KeyM_VerifyCertificates checks exactly one pair consisting of a lower and upper certificate ([SWS_KeyM_00059]).
  • KeyM_VerifyCertificate determines the chain for a set certificate itself from the stored certificates ([SWS_KeyM_00060]).
  • KeyM_VerifyCertificateChain checks a chain provided by the caller and sorted in PKI order ([SWS_KeyM_00061]).

If the call returns E_OK, the configured KeyMCertificateVerifyCallbackNotificationFunc reports the result later as KeyM_CertificateStatusType ([SWS_KeyM_00153], [SWS_KeyM_00073]).

Sequence diagram: A working certificate is set, parsed, asynchronously verified; the public key is subsequently set and validated in the CSM, and the result is reported via callback. Sources: SWS KeyM (Fig. 9.4) p. 119, [SWS_KeyM_00060], [SWS_KeyM_00170], [SWS_KeyM_00153]

Certificate services and access to certificate elements

If KeyMServiceCertificateFunctionEnabled and KeyMCertificateManagerEnabled are set, the certificate submodule offers KeyM_ServiceCertificate. Via this, the key master introduces or updates persistently stored certificates ([SWS_KeyM_00021], [SWS_KeyM_00056]). The operation is selected via KeyM_ServiceCertificateType ([SWS_KeyM_00039]):

  • request CSR or restore signed CSR,
  • set or update root or intermediate certificate,
  • provide revocation list,
  • vendor-specific extensions in the reserved range 0x80–0x9F.

The operation runs asynchronously and ends with KeyM_ServiceCertificateCallbackNotification ([SWS_KeyM_00149], [SWS_KeyM_00152]). Optionally, the key handler KeyM_KH_ServiceCertificate can be integrated ([SWS_KeyM_00072]).

Differences from later releases: These add KeyM_ServiceCertificateByCertId and reduce the callback to CertId and Result (SWS KeyM p. 92). For R20-11, the signature with ResultDataLength and ResultDataPtr applies ([SWS_KeyM_00147]). Installation and update attempts for root and intermediate certificates are standardized as security events KEYM_SEV_INST_ROOT_CERT_OP through KEYM_SEV_UPD_INTERMEDIATE_CERT_OP ([SWS_KeyM_00172]).

Sequence diagram: A root or intermediate certificate is introduced via KeyM_ServiceCertificate, parsed, checked for validity period, and stored in NvM or CSM depending on configuration; completion is reported by the service callback. Sources: SWS KeyM (Fig. 9.5) p. 120, [SWS_KeyM_00056], [SWS_KeyM_00149], [SWS_KeyM_00147]

KeyM_CertElementGet reads the contents of parsed certificates based on the configured object ID ([SWS_KeyM_00063], [SWS_KeyM_00127]). Elements with multiple occurrences can be traversed in two ways:

  • using KeyM_CertElementGetFirst/KeyM_CertElementGetNext and a KeyM_CertElementIteratorType held by the caller, which must remain unchanged until the end ([SWS_KeyM_00064], [SWS_KeyM_00065], [SWS_KeyM_00042]),
  • index-based using KeyM_CertificateElementGetCount and KeyM_CertificateElementGetByIndex ([SWS_KeyM_91015], [SWS_KeyM_91014]).

Iteration is permitted only for elements with KeyMCertificateElementHasIteration = TRUE ([SWS_KeyM_00148]).

Key update as a Start–Prepare–Update–Finalize session

The crypto key submodule can be operated in a session-like manner. KeyM_Start opens the session, KeyM_Finalize closes it; in between, operations such as KeyM_Prepare and KeyM_Update are accepted ([SWS_KeyM_00050], [SWS_KeyM_00053], SWS KeyM p. 25). KeyM_StartType distinguishes the OEM production mode with higher privileges from the workshop mode ([SWS_KeyM_00038]).

If a key handler is activated, KeyM_Start passes the parameters to KeyM_KH_Start and adopts its return value. In this way, vendor-specific signature verifications can be implemented, for example ([SWS_KeyM_00067], SWS KeyM p. 25). Accordingly, KeyM_Prepare and KeyM_Finalize delegate to KeyM_KH_Prepare and KeyM_KH_Finalize, respectively ([SWS_KeyM_00068], [SWS_KeyM_00070]). Completion of the finalization is reported by KeyM_CryptoKeyFinalizeCallbackNotification if KeyMCryptoKeyStartFinalizeFunctionEnabled is set ([SWS_KeyM_00080], [SWS_KeyM_00079]).

Sequence diagram: The key session opens with KeyM_Start, prepares with KeyM_Prepare, updates asynchronously with KeyM_Update, and closes with KeyM_Finalize; key handlers are engaged depending on configuration. Sources: [SWS_KeyM_00050], [SWS_KeyM_00067], [SWS_KeyM_00068], [SWS_KeyM_00077], [SWS_KeyM_00080], SWS KeyM (Fig. 9.2) p. 117

KeyM_Update operates asynchronously ([SWS_KeyM_00052]). KeyM finds the target key in one of two ways:

  • via the name in KeyMCryptoKeyName ([SWS_KeyM_00091]),
  • without a valid name, via bits 121..124 of the request data interpreted as SHE-M1M2M3, matched against KeyMCryptoKeyCryptoProps ([SWS_KeyM_00154]).

Without a match and without a key handler, the call ends with KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH ([SWS_KeyM_00155]). With a key handler, the update proceeds as follows:

  1. KeyM calls KeyM_KH_Update with the found key or 0xFFFFFFFFul ([SWS_KeyM_00092]), providing an internal buffer in the process ([SWS_KeyM_00097]).
  2. If the handler reports KEYM_KH_UPDATE_KEY_UPDATE_REPEAT with data, KeyM stores or derives the key in the CSM and calls the handler again ([SWS_KeyM_00096], [SWS_KeyM_00055]).
  3. If the handler reports KEYM_KH_UPDATE_FINISH, KeyM copies the result into the buffer of the caller and calls KeyM_CryptoKeyUpdateCallbackNotification ([SWS_KeyM_00093]).

Until this callback, the caller must not modify the result buffer ([SWS_KeyM_00156]).

Activity diagram: KeyM_Update determines the target key via name or SHE data and processes it directly or in a key handler loop up to KEYM_KH_UPDATE_FINISH. Sources: [SWS_KeyM_00091], [SWS_KeyM_00092], [SWS_KeyM_00093], [SWS_KeyM_00096], [SWS_KeyM_00154], [SWS_KeyM_00155]

Depending on the configuration, KeyM_Verify verifies keys synchronously. If KeyMCryptoKeyVerifyAsyncMode = TRUE, the verification runs asynchronously, and the result is provided via KeyM_CryptoKeyVerifyCallbackNotification ([SWS_KeyM_00054], [SWS_KeyM_00151], [SWS_KeyM_00081]).

Module operation: initialization, timing, and invocation rules

KeyM_Init initializes the module ([SWS_KeyM_00043]). The configuration pointer must always be NULL_PTR ([SWS_KeyM_00158]), although the parameter description specifies a post-build configuration set. Interpretation: In R20-11, the configuration is therefore presumably not passed via this pointer in practice. KeyM_Deinit sets the module to the uninitialized state ([SWS_KeyM_00047]). The version starting from R23-11 additionally requires active erasing of key material in RAM (SWS KeyM p. 49).

KeyM_MainFunction is called periodically at the configured interval ([SWS_KeyM_00074]). KeyM_MainBackgroundFunction runs during idle times of a preemptive operating system and is suitable for time-consuming synchronous functions such as KeyM_KH_Update ([SWS_KeyM_00075]). Presumably, these functions advance the asynchronous services: the APIs report their acceptance with E_OK, and their completion via a callback ([SWS_KeyM_00060], [SWS_KeyM_00052]). The services are entirely non-reentrant; the iterator functions are reentrant only per iterator ([SWS_KeyM_00057], [SWS_KeyM_00064]). Callback names are configurable and are included via KeyM_Externals.h ([SWS_KeyM_00073], SWS KeyM p. 91).

Behavior in the event of an error

With development error detection enabled, KeyM checks upon each call ([SWS_KeyM_00144], [SWS_KeyM_00145], [SWS_KeyM_00146], [SWS_KeyM_00036]):

  • the initialization (KEYM_E_UNINIT),
  • the buffer sizes (KEYM_E_SMALL_BUFFER),
  • unexpected NULL pointers (KEYM_E_PARAM_POINTER).

If the referenced certificate has the storage class KEYM_STORAGE_IN_CSM or KEYM_STORAGE_IN_NVM, the specification requires KEYM_E_CONFIG_FAILURE, without development mode E_NOT_OK ([SWS_KeyM_00166]).

Synchronous return values use KeyM-specific values ([SWS_KeyM_00040]):

  • KEYM_E_BUSY: other jobs are still running,
  • KEYM_E_PENDING: job accepted, processing asynchronous,
  • KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH, KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH, and KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_INVALID.

Certificate functions add further codes. KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY stands for empty slots, KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_READ_FAIL for denied access, and KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST for an invalid parent certificate ([SWS_KeyM_00058], [SWS_KeyM_00060], SWS KeyM p. 66). Non-iterable elements return KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID ([SWS_KeyM_00148]). In case of failure, KeyM_CertElementGet sets the output length to zero ([SWS_KeyM_00063], SWS KeyM p. 71).

Asynchronous errors arrive in the callback. KeyM_ResultType distinguishes, among others, KEYM_RT_NOT_OK, KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_INVALID, KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_WRITE_FAIL, KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_UPDATE_FAIL, and KEYM_RT_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST ([SWS_KeyM_91008]). Certificate checks deliver the detailed status from KeyM_CertificateStatusType ([SWS_KeyM_00073], [SWS_KeyM_91003]).

A failed chain check is additionally the security event KEYM_SEV_CERT_VERIF_FAILED (ID 5) ([SWS_KeyM_00172]). It is reported to the IdsM only if KeyMEnableSecurityEventReporting = TRUE. Later releases name the event SEV_CERT_CHAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED (SWS KeyM p. 38); for R20-11, the name from [SWS_KeyM_00172] applies.

Further detailed evidence

  • [SWS_KeyM_00050], [SWS_KeyM_00053], [SWS_KeyM_00067], [SWS_KeyM_00070]: Session framework and delegation to key handlers.
  • [SWS_KeyM_00091], [SWS_KeyM_00093], [SWS_KeyM_00096], [SWS_KeyM_00097], [SWS_KeyM_00156]: Execution sequence and buffer rules of KeyM_Update.
  • [SWS_KeyM_00170], [SWS_KeyM_00153]: Completion of a certificate verification with key release in the CSM.
  • [SWS_KeyM_91003] and SWS KeyM (Fig. 7.4) p. 24: Certificate status in the R20-11 version.
  • [SWS_KeyM_00021], [SWS_KeyM_00039], [SWS_KeyM_00152]: Service certificate operations.
  • [SWS_KeyM_00036], [SWS_KeyM_00040], [SWS_KeyM_91008]: Error and result codes.
  • SWS KeyM p. 37: describes the offloading of certificate operations via CSM custom jobs. This section originates from R23-11/R25-11, and the payload contains no R20-11 requirements for it; it is therefore not treated as a feature of R20-11 here.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 9a18ff4ee970 Provenance

The function KeyM_Deinit ([SWS_KeyM_00047]) resets the key management module to the uninitialized state. It has the service ID 0x02 and is made available via the header KeyM.h.

Usage and Semantics

  • Call context and parameters: The function has the signature void KeyM_Deinit (void);. It expects no input parameters (neither in, inout nor out) and returns no return value.
  • Synchronicity: Execution is synchronous (Synchronous).
  • Concurrency: The function is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) and therefore must not be executed concurrently or preemptively.

Interaction and Error Handling

Calling KeyM_Deinit transitions the module into the state prior to initialization. This entails the following interactions in the overall system:

  • If development error detection is active, the Key Manager checks according to [SWS_KeyM_00144] on each function call whether the module has been initialized with KeyM_Init() and not yet deinitialized via KeyM_Deinit().
  • If a function of the Key Manager is called after execution of KeyM_Deinit without prior re-initialization, the development error KEYM_E_UNINIT is reported ([SWS_KeyM_00144]).

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

Std_ReturnType KeyM_Start (KeyM_StartType StartType, const uint8* Request Data, uint16 Request Data Length, uint8* Response Data, uint16* Response Data Length);

This function is optional and only used if the configuration item Key MCrypto Key Start Finalize Function Enabled is set to true. It intents to allow key update operation.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 8f7ecc59ddcd Provenance

Usage and Configuration

The function KeyM_Start ([SWS_KeyM_00050], AUTOSAR_SWS_KeyManager p. 35) is optional and only available if the configuration parameter KeyMCryptoKeyStartFinalizeFunctionEnabled is set to true. Its purpose is to permit subsequent key update operations. The function is provided via the header KeyM.h and operates synchronously.

  • StartType (in): Defines the mode in which the key operation is to be executed.
  • RequestData (in) and RequestDataLength (in): Pointer to the data passed with the request (e.g. a signature) as well as its length in bytes.
  • ResponseDataLength (inout): Passes on input the maximum byte amount available in the output buffer and returns on output the actual number of written bytes.
  • ResponseData (out): Buffer to receive the payload data returned by the function.

Return Values and Error Handling

The return value of type Std_ReturnType signals the result of the initialization:

  • E_OK: The start operation was successfully executed; key updates are now permitted.
  • E_NOT_OK: The start operation was rejected.
  • KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH: A passed parameter does not match the expected value.
  • KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH: The size of a passed parameter is incorrect.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_KeyM_00050], the service function (Service ID 0x04) is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). Callers must therefore ensure that no concurrent calls to KeyM_Start occur.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.

function KeyM_Prepare [SWS_KeyM_00051] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType KeyM_Prepare (const uint8* Request Data, uint16 Request Data Length, uint8* Response Data, uint16* Response Data Length);

This function is used to prepare a key update operation. The main intent is to provide information for the key operation to the key server. Other operations may start the negotiation for a common secret that is used further to derive key material. This function is only av ailable if Key MCrypto Key Prepare Function Enabled is set to TRUE.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 57620615e44b Provenance

According to [SWS_KeyM_00051], function KeyM_Prepare serves to prepare a key update (AUTOSAR_SWS_KeyManager p. 36). The primary purpose is to provide required information for the key operation to the key server or to start a negotiation of a common secret from which key material is derived in the further course. The function is available only if the configuration parameter KeyMCryptoKeyPrepareFunctionEnabled is set to TRUE, and is declared via header KeyM.h.

Call Context and Parameters

The call is executed with service ID 0x05. The function signature is specified as synchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). The following parameters are processed:

  • Request Data (IN): Pointer to the data transmitted with the request.
  • Request Data Length (IN): Length of the data array in Request Data.

The return value of type Std_ReturnType provides information about the acceptance of the job or errors that occurred [SWS_KeyM_00053]:

Return Values and Error Handling

If the request is accepted successfully, the function returns E_OK; the actual certificate verification is subsequently executed in the background. Otherwise, the operation is rejected and one of the following error values is returned:

  • KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH: The passed certificate ID (CertId) is invalid.

The synchronous function KeyM_CertElementGetNext ([SWS_KeyM_00065]) reads subsequent data of a certificate element if an element contains multiple data records to be retrieved sequentially. A prerequisite for the call is that KeyM_CertElementGetFirst() has previously been called at least once. The declaration is provided via the header file KeyM.h.

Parameters and buffers

  • CertElementIterator (inout): Pointer to an iterator structure provided by the caller. It must neither be modified nor released by the application during the entire iteration process ([SWS_KeyM_00065]).
  • CertElementData (out): Pointer to the buffer allocated by the caller, into which the element data is copied upon successful execution.
  • CertElementDataLength (inout): Passes on the input side the maximum length of the data buffer. Upon return of E_OK, the value is overwritten with the actually written byte length ([SWS_KeyM_00065]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The function returns the following status values via type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_KeyM_00065]):

  • E_OK: Element successfully found, data provided in the buffer, and iterator updated accordingly.
  • E_NOT_OK: Element data was not found. The iterator must no longer be used for any further calls.
  • KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH: The provided data buffer is too small for the certificate element.
  • KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH: Invalid certificate ID or invalid certificate element ID.
  • KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY: No certificate data is available (certificate is empty).
  • KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID: The certificate is invalid or was not successfully verified.

Concurrency and Limitations

KeyM_CertElementGetNext operates synchronously and is reentrant for exactly one iterator ([SWS_KeyM_00065]). Parallel calls must therefore not use the same iterator.

  • ResponseData (out): Pointer to the buffer for receiving the returned data ([SWS_KeyM_00070]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The function call returns a status of type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_KeyM_00070]):

  • E_OK: The operation was accepted and is processed further internally; results are provided via a callback.
  • E_NOT_OK: The operation was rejected due to an internal error.

  • KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH: A passed parameter does not match the expected value.
  • KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH: The specified parameter size does not match.

function KeyM_CryptoKeyUpdateCallbackNotification [SWS_KeyM_00077] 📄 PDF

void KeyM_CryptoKeyUpdateCallbackNotification (KeyM_ResultType Result, uint16 Result Data Length, const uint8* Result DataPtr);

Notifies the application that a crypto key update operation has been finished. This function is used by the key manager.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 9bad93ada4f7 Provenance

Usage and purpose

The callback function [SWS_KeyM_00077] is called by the Key Manager to notify the higher-level application of the completion of a key update (crypto key update operation). It is specified as synchronous and reentrant, has no return value (void), and is declared via the header file KeyM_Externals.h.

Parameters

  • Result: Contains the overall result of the update operation.
  • ResultDataLength: Indicates the length of the resulting result data of this operation, if present.
  • ResultDataPtr: Pointer to the generated result data.

Interaction and Buffer Management

The buffer management and the notification sequence are strictly coupled to the update process:

  • According to [SWS_KeyM_00156], the calling function of KeyM_Update() must pass a buffer pointer ResultDataPtr. Provided that KeyM_Update() accepts the operation with E_OK, this buffer must not be touched by the caller until the callback [SWS_KeyM_00077] has occurred. All results of KeyM_Update() are copied into this buffer, and the same pointer is passed back to the callback as ResultDataPtr.
  • According to [SWS_KeyM_00093], the notification [SWS_KeyM_00077] is triggered by the function KeyM_Update() as soon as the key handler returns and terminates the operation with KEYM_KH_UPDATE_FINISH. In doing so, the result data from KeyM_KH_Update::ResultDataPtr is transferred into the buffer provided by KeyM_Update::ResultDataPtr, and the return value of the key handler is used.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

According to [SWS_KeyM_00039], the enumeration type KeyM_ServiceCertificateType specifies the requested service operation as well as the type of certificate information provided within the scope of a function. The type is available via the header file Rte_KeyM_Type.h.

Usage and Value Range

The defined constants control administrative certificate operations between key server and key client:

  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_REQUEST_CSR (0x01): Request from the key server to generate a certificate at the key client.
  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_SIGNED_CSR (0x02): Retransmission of a certificate previously received and signed by the certificate authority (CA).
  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_SET_ROOT (0x03): Installation of a new root certificate.
  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_ROOT (0x04): Update of an existing root certificate.
  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_SET_INTERMEDIATE (0x05): Installation of a new intermediate or CA certificate.
  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_INTERMEDIATE (0x06): Update of an existing intermediate or CA certificate.
  • KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_CRL (0x07): Provision or update of a certificate revocation list (Certificate Revocation List).
  • 0x80 to 0x9F: Reserved value range for user-specific extensions.

Sequence Conditions and Restrictions

According to [SWS_KeyM_00039], an explicit precondition applies to operation KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_SET_INTERMEDIATE: The parent root certificate must have been stored in advance to ensure successful verification of the CA certificate.

Interpretation: Since KeyM_ServiceCertificateType represents a pure type definition, the element itself specifies no runtime contexts, error codes, or reentrancy properties of its own; these are likely to arise only from the respective functions that use this type as an input parameter.

Type KeyM_CertificateStatusType.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: dc730981e3e7 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The type KeyM_CertificateStatusType is defined as an enumeration and represents the result of certificate checks as well as the current processing status of a certificate in the Key Manager ([SWS_KeyM_91003]). The type is available via the header Rte_KeyM_Type.h ([SWS_KeyM_91003]).

Status Values and Error Interpretation

The enumeration values reflect both regular processing states and specific verification errors ([SWS_KeyM_91003]):

  • KEYM_CERTIFICATE_VALID (0x00): Certificate successfully parsed and verified.
  • KEYM_CERTIFICATE_INVALID (0x01): Certificate invalid (unspecified error).
  • KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_PARSED (0x02): Not parsed so far.
  • KEYM_CERTIFICATE_PARSED_NOT_VALIDATED (0x03): Certificate parsed, but not yet validated.
  • KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_AVAILABLE (0x04): Certificate not set.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_VALIDITY_PERIOD_FAIL (0x05): Validity period invalid.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_SIGNATURE_FAIL (0x06): Signature check failed.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST (0x07): Chain of trust invalid.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_TYPE (0x08): Invalid certificate type.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_FORMAT (0x09): Invalid format.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_CONTENT (0x0A): Invalid content.
  • KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_REVOKED (0x0B): Certificate check failed due to invalid scope or revocation.

Callers typically evaluate the status to determine whether a certificate has already been checked (0x02, 0x03), is ready for use (0x00), or due to which specific cause the verification was rejected ([SWS_KeyM_91003]).

The enumeration defines the following result and error values for asynchronous operations [SWS_KeyM_91008]:

  • KEYM_RT_OK (0x00): The key management operation was executed successfully [SWS_KeyM_91008].
  • KEYM_RT_NOT_OK (0x01): General error during execution of the key management operation [SWS_KeyM_91008].
  • KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_INVALID (0x02): The key or certificate is invalid and cannot be used for the operation [SWS_KeyM_91008].
  • KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_WRITE_FAIL (0x03): The key or certificate could not be written to the memory provided for it [SWS_KeyM_91008].
  • KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_UPDATE_FAIL (0x04): General error while updating a key or certificate that could not be specified by more specific error codes [SWS_KeyM_91008].
  • KEYM_RT_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST (0x05): The verification of the certificate failed because the chain of trust is invalid [SWS_KeyM_91008].

Usage and Error Handling

Callers of asynchronous key management services use these return values for differentiated evaluation of the operation result [SWS_KeyM_91008]. In addition to the general error status KEYM_RT_NOT_OK, the type allows a targeted distinction between storage errors (KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_WRITE_FAIL), invalid keys or certificates (KEYM_RT_KEY_CERT_INVALID), and validation errors within the chain of trust (KEYM_RT_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST) [SWS_KeyM_91008].

  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00039">[SWS_KeyM_00039]</a>, the enumeration type <code>KeyM_ServiceCertificateType</code> specifies the requested service operation as well as the type of certificate information provided within the scope of a function. The type is available via the header file <code>Rte_KeyM_Type.h</code>.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Value Range</h4>
  <p>The defined constants control administrative certificate operations between key server and key client:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_REQUEST_CSR</code> (0x01): Request from the key server to generate a certificate at the key client.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_SIGNED_CSR</code> (0x02): Retransmission of a certificate previously received and signed by the certificate authority (CA).</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_SET_ROOT</code> (0x03): Installation of a new root certificate.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_ROOT</code> (0x04): Update of an existing root certificate.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_SET_INTERMEDIATE</code> (0x05): Installation of a new intermediate or CA certificate.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_INTERMEDIATE</code> (0x06): Update of an existing intermediate or CA certificate.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_UPDATE_CRL</code> (0x07): Provision or update of a certificate revocation list (Certificate Revocation List).</li>
    <li><code>0x80</code> to <code>0x9F</code>: Reserved value range for user-specific extensions.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Sequence Conditions and Restrictions</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00039">[SWS_KeyM_00039]</a>, an explicit precondition applies to operation <code>KEYM_SERVICE_CERT_SET_INTERMEDIATE</code>: The parent root certificate must have been stored in advance to ensure successful verification of the CA certificate.</p>
  <p>Interpretation: Since <code>KeyM_ServiceCertificateType</code> represents a pure type definition, the element itself specifies no runtime contexts, error codes, or reentrancy properties of its own; these are likely to arise only from the respective functions that use this type as an input parameter.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>

<h4>Usage of <code>KeyM_CertDataType</code></h4>
<p>The data structure <code>KeyM_CertDataType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00041" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00041">[SWS_KeyM_00041]</a>) serves to exchange certificate data via interface functions of module <code>KeyM</code>. It is provided via the header file <code>KeyM.h</code> and bundles the raw data of a certificate with the corresponding length specification.</p>

<p>The structure defines two elements (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00041" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00041">[SWS_KeyM_00041]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>certDataLength</code> (type <code>uint32</code>): Determines the length of the provided certificate data.</li>
<li><code>certData</code> (type <code>void*</code>): Pointer to the certificate data located in a local data area of the caller.</li>
</ul>

<p>Since <code>certData</code> points to a local data area of the caller, the caller is likely to be responsible for ensuring that the referenced buffer remains allocated and unmodified for the entire duration of the interface call (interpretation: memory management and buffer validity are the responsibility of the caller). In addition, <code>certDataLength</code> should correspond exactly to the size of the referenced memory area in order to avoid faulty accesses during processing.</p>

<p>Since the specification in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00041" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00041">[SWS_KeyM_00041]</a> defines no error codes, DET/DEM messages, or concurrency requirements, aspects such as reentrancy and error handling depend on the specific functions that use <code>KeyM_CertDataType</code> as an input parameter.</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00042" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00042">[SWS_KeyM_00042]</a>, the data structure <code>KeyM_CertElementIteratorType</code> serves to iterate over multiple elements of a certificate. The type is specified as <code>Structure</code> and is provided via the header <code>KeyM.h</code>.</p>
<p>Since the concrete elements and contents of the data structure are implementation-specific (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00042" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00042">[SWS_KeyM_00042]</a>), direct read or write access to internal structure components by calling modules is not permitted. Interpretation: The structure is likely to function as an opaque state storage for iteration steps whose instances are initialized, advanced, and evaluated exclusively via associated certificate functions of module <code>KeyM</code>.</p>
<h4>Restrictions and Concurrency</h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>Encapsulation:</strong> Since the internal layout is implemented in a vendor-specific manner, the caller must treat the iterator as an abstract object in order not to jeopardize portability across different AUTOSAR implementations.</li>
<li><strong>Concurrency:</strong> If certificate elements are iterated simultaneously from different execution contexts or tasks, external synchronization will likely be required for the same instance of <code>KeyM_CertElementIteratorType</code> due to the lack of specified internal protection mechanisms.</li>
</ul>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="9a18ff4ee970779dbfd0c06ec2937001b734a3f8ad36d31ba5b741e6567bfd41" data-trace-output="0ae75c053a183fdbdbcb5f7c232c28db61920a53bab42b5b4f31f3f53ab6751b" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The function <code>KeyM_Deinit</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00047" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00047">[SWS_KeyM_00047]</a>) resets the key management module to the uninitialized state. It has the service ID <code>0x02</code> and is made available via the header <code>KeyM.h</code>.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Call context and parameters:</strong> The function has the signature <code>void KeyM_Deinit (void);</code>. It expects no input parameters (neither <em>in</em>, <em>inout</em> nor <em>out</em>) and returns no return value.</li>
    <li><strong>Synchronicity:</strong> Execution is synchronous (<code>Synchronous</code>).</li>
    <li><strong>Concurrency:</strong> The function is specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) and therefore must not be executed concurrently or preemptively.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>Calling <code>KeyM_Deinit</code> transitions the module into the state prior to initialization. This entails the following interactions in the overall system:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>If development error detection is active, the Key Manager checks according to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00144" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00144">[SWS_KeyM_00144]</a> on each function call whether the module has been initialized with <code>KeyM_Init()</code> and not yet deinitialized via <code>KeyM_Deinit()</code>.</li>

  <h4>Usage and Configuration</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>KeyM_Start</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00050" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00050">[SWS_KeyM_00050]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=907&amp;page=35">AUTOSAR_SWS_KeyManager p. 35</a>) is optional and only available if the configuration parameter <code>KeyMCryptoKeyStartFinalizeFunctionEnabled</code> is set to <code>true</code>. Its purpose is to permit subsequent key update operations. The function is provided via the header <code>KeyM.h</code> and operates synchronously.
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>StartType</code> (in): Defines the mode in which the key operation is to be executed.</li>
    <li><code>RequestData</code> (in) and <code>RequestDataLength</code> (in): Pointer to the data passed with the request (e.g. a signature) as well as its length in bytes.</li>
    <li><code>ResponseDataLength</code> (inout): Passes on input the maximum byte amount available in the output buffer and returns on output the actual number of written bytes.</li>
    <li><code>ResponseData</code> (out): Buffer to receive the payload data returned by the function.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> signals the result of the initialization:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The start operation was successfully executed; key updates are now permitted.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The start operation was rejected.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: A passed parameter does not match the expected value.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The size of a passed parameter is incorrect.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00050" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00050">[SWS_KeyM_00050]</a>, the service function (Service ID <code>0x04</code>) is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). Callers must therefore ensure that no concurrent calls to <code>KeyM_Start</code> occur.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">
    This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.
  </p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="2c76fcd98f23cffd94aee0acf3802214418d6728e2ae658e1a951796de4ffa0f" data-trace-output="60f548f8ee71b467de5028d403affc3a72af2fcebad9f020100bbb7028bdca0f" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>KeyM_Finalize</code> concludes update operations for cryptographic keys and returns the key operation back to the idle state (idle mode) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>. Execution is asynchronous and non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.
  </p>
  <p>
    Accompanying request data is passed via <code>RequestDataPtr</code> and <code>RequestDataLength</code>. The buffer <code>ResponseDataPtr</code> receives the return data. The in/out parameter <code>ResponseMaxDataLength</code> initially specifies the maximum available buffer size; upon completion it returns the actual data length or remains unchanged during asynchronous processing after returning <code>E_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.
  </p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> provides information about the acceptance of the job or errors that occurred <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The operation was accepted and is processed asynchronously internally; results are provided via a callback <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: Rejection of the operation due to an internal error <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_BUSY</code>: The Key Manager is currently busy with other tasks <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: A parameter does not match the expected value <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The parameter size differs <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Constraints</h4>
  <p>
    The function is only available if <code>KeyMCryptoKeyStartFinalizeFunctionEnabled</code> is configured to <code>TRUE</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>. It is typically used in conjunction with <code>KeyM_Start</code>. After calling <code>KeyM_Finalize</code>, further preparation or update operations (Prepare/Update) are only accepted again once a new <code>KeyM_Start</code> operation has been initialized <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>. Additionally, in the course of finalization, the updated key material is persistently stored and transitioned to the valid state via <code>Csm_KeySetValid</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00053" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00053">[SWS_KeyM_00053]</a>.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>
</div>

<p>The synchronous function <code>KeyM_SetCertificate</code> serves to pass certificate data to the module Key Manager (<code>KeyM</code>) in order to temporarily store the specified certificate there <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>. The declaration is available via the header <code>KeyM.h</code>, and the Service ID <code>0x0a</code> is assigned to the service <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</p>
<h4>use</h4>
<p>The call to <code>KeyM_SetCertificate</code> expects two input parameters <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>CertId</code>: Denotes the identifier of the certificate concerned of type <code>KeyM_CertificateIdType</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</li>
<li><code>CertificateDataPtr</code>: Pointer to a structure of type <code>KeyM_CertDataType</code> that contains the certificate data to be provided <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Neither input/output parameters nor pure output parameters are defined <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</p>
<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>The function returns a value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>, which reflects the processing status <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The certificate was successfully accepted <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The certificate could not be set <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</li>
<li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: At least one passed parameter does not match the expected value <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</li>
<li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The size of the passed parameters does not match <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>The function is executed synchronously and is classified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00057">[SWS_KeyM_00057]</a>.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The function <code>KeyM_GetCertificate</code> provides certificate data synchronously and is available via the header file <code>KeyM.h</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>. The identifier of the requested certificate is passed via the input parameter <code>CertId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>. Via the input/output parameter <code>CertificateDataPtr</code>, the caller passes a pointer to a certificate data structure of type <code>KeyM_CertDataType</code> whose internal buffer must be provided by the caller <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>. Upon invocation, the length field of the structure indicates the maximum buffer size; upon successful execution (<code>E_OK</code>), it indicates the actual data length of the written certificate <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> provides specific feedback codes for evaluation <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: Certificate data is present and has been provided <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: Operation not accepted due to an internal error <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: Invalid certificate ID (<code>CertId</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The provided buffer is too small for the certificate <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: No certificate data available, the certificate slot is empty <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_READ_FAIL</code>: Access denied, certificate cannot be read out <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) and has the Service ID <code>0x0b</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00058" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00058">[SWS_KeyM_00058]</a>.</p>

  <p>The function <code>KeyM_VerifyCertificates</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00059" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00059">[SWS_KeyM_00059]</a>) serves for mutual verification of two internally stored and already parsed certificates. Specifically, it is validated whether the lower certificate of the chain referenced via <code>CertId</code> was signed by the upper certificate designated with <code>CertUpperId</code>. The verification is limited exclusively to these two certificates.</p>

  <p>Execution is asynchronous (<code>Asynchronous</code>) and specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00059" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00059">[SWS_KeyM_00059]</a>). After successful acceptance of the verification request, the synchronous return value <code>E_OK</code> signals that verification has been started in the background. The actual result of the verification is communicated to the caller via the configured callback function <code>KeyMCertificateVerifyCallbackNotificationFunc</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00153" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00153">[SWS_KeyM_00153]</a>).</p>

  <p>If the operation request is rejected, the synchronous call returns one of the following error codes (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00059" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00059">[SWS_KeyM_00059]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_BUSY</code>: The Key Manager is already executing other requests; the verification cannot be accepted yet.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: At least one of the specified certificate IDs is invalid.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: One of the referenced certificate slots does not contain a certificate.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST</code>: The parent certificate (<code>CertUpperId</code>) is invalid.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: An internal error prevented acceptance of the request.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="3ad931b6bb9229084596e31f1ca7bd839058e531cc5fc8a95407ee8712498f0a" data-trace-output="d56c5731f1c76ed4fa2f5dfee78d144b2a0844b86aef3803596150e5ce1eb337" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The function <code>KeyM_VerifyCertificate</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00060" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00060">[SWS_KeyM_00060]</a>) serves for the asynchronous verification of a certificate previously provided via <code>KeyM_SetCertificate()</code> against already stored certificates of other certificate IDs. As input parameter, <code>CertId</code> (type <code>KeyM_CertificateIdType</code>) is passed, which holds the identifier of the certificate to be verified. The interface is declared via the header <code>KeyM.h</code>.</p>

<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>If the request is accepted successfully, the function returns <code>E_OK</code>; the actual certificate verification is subsequently executed in the background. Otherwise, the operation is rejected and one of the following error values is returned:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>KEYM_E_BUSY</code>: The <code>KeyM</code> is currently busy with other requests, which is why validation cannot be performed yet.</li>
<li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: The passed certificate ID (<code>CertId</code>) is invalid.</li>
<li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: At least one of the required certificate slots is empty.</li>
<li><code>KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST</code>: A parent certificate within the chain of trust is invalid.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The operation was not accepted due to an internal error.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>The function is defined as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00060" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00060">[SWS_KeyM_00060]</a>). Callers must therefore ensure that calls to <code>KeyM_VerifyCertificate</code> do not occur concurrently.</p>

<h4>Interaction</h4>
<p>If the verification request was successfully acknowledged with <code>E_OK</code> and a callback function is configured under <code>KeyMCertificateVerifyCallbackNotificationFunc</code>, it is called to provide the final result of the background verification for the certificate concerned (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00153" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00153">[SWS_KeyM_00153]</a>).</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>KeyM_VerifyCertificateChain</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00061">[SWS_KeyM_00061]</a>) serves for asynchronous certificate verification based on a list of passed certificates. The parameter <code>CertId</code> designates the last certificate of the certificate chain. Via <code>certChainData</code>, a pointer to a certificate array sorted according to PKI order is passed, whose number of elements is determined by <code>NumberOfCertificates</code>. As a prerequisite, the certificate to be verified must have been previously stored via <code>KeyM_SetCertificate()</code>. In addition, the root certificate must either be contained in the passed list or already assigned to one of the other certificates.
  </p>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    If the verification request is accepted, the call returns <code>E_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00061">[SWS_KeyM_00061]</a>). If validation cannot be initiated, the function returns specific error values:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_BUSY</code>: The Key Manager is busy with other tasks; the verification cannot be executed yet.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: The specified certificate ID (<code>CertId</code>) is invalid.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: At least one of the required certificate slots is unoccupied.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST</code>: A parent certificate within the chain of trust is invalid.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: An internal error prevented acceptance of the operation.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Interaction</h4>
  <p>
    The function is specified as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00061">[SWS_KeyM_00061]</a>). After successful acceptance with <code>E_OK</code>, verification runs in the background. The result of the verification is transmitted asynchronously to the application via the configured callback <code>KeyMCertificateVerifyCallbackNotificationFunc</code> for the certificate concerned (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00153" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00153">[SWS_KeyM_00153]</a>).
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <p>
    The function <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00063" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00063">[SWS_KeyM_00063]</a> serves to synchronously read out the content of a specific certificate element. It is used when exactly one element is assigned to the identifier stored in the certificate configuration (e.g. Object Identifier, OID).
  </p>
  <p>
    <strong>Usage and buffer passing:</strong> The caller must provide the data buffer <code>CertElementData</code> itself and pass its maximum capacity via the pointer <code>CertElementDataLength</code>. If the data is determined successfully, the service copies it into the buffer, overwrites <code>CertElementDataLength</code> with the actual data length, and returns <code>E_OK</code>. For any different return value, <code>CertElementDataLength</code> is set to the value zero.
  </p>
  <p>
    <strong>Error handling:</strong> Possible error conditions are reported in a differentiated manner via the return type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: The passed certificate ID (<code>CertId</code>) or element ID (<code>CertElementId</code>) is invalid.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The data buffer provided by the caller is too small for the certificate element.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: The addressed certificate slot is empty; no certificate data is present.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_INVALID</code>: The certificate is invalid or has not yet been verified.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The requested element data was not found.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>
    <strong>Concurrency and integration:</strong> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00063" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00063">[SWS_KeyM_00063]</a> is specified as synchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). Callers must therefore ensure that concurrent calls are avoided. The interface is provided via the header <code>KeyM.h</code>.
  </p>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>KeyM_CertElementGetFirst</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00064">[SWS_KeyM_00064]</a>) serves to initialize the iterative reading of a certificate data element. It always retrieves the top element of the certificate element specified via <code>CertElementId</code> from the certificate specified by <code>CertId</code> and initializes the iterator structure <code>CertElementIterator</code>. The caller provides the output buffer <code>CertElementData</code> as well as the maximum buffer size via <code>CertElementDataLength</code>; upon successful return (<code>E_OK</code>), the actual data length is written back to <code>CertElementDataLength</code>.</p>

  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>In case of success, the function returns <code>E_OK</code>. If the element data could not be found, <code>E_NOT_OK</code> is returned; the iterator must then not be used for subsequent calls. Specific return values in case of error are:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: The passed <code>CertId</code> or <code>CertElementId</code> is invalid.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The provided data buffer is too small for the certificate element.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: The certificate contains no data or is empty.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID</code>: The certificate is invalid or verification was not successful.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is reentrant with respect to a single iterator (<em>Reentrant for one iterator</em>). The structure <code>CertElementIterator</code> allocated and managed by the caller must neither be destroyed nor modified by the application as long as not all associated elements have been retrieved via <code>KeyM_CertElementGetNext()</code>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Flow</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous function <code>KeyM_CertElementGetNext</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00065">[SWS_KeyM_00065]</a>) reads subsequent data of a certificate element if an element contains multiple data records to be retrieved sequentially. A prerequisite for the call is that <code>KeyM_CertElementGetFirst()</code> has previously been called at least once. The declaration is provided via the header file <code>KeyM.h</code>.
  </p>
  <h4>Parameters and buffers</h4>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <code>CertElementIterator</code> (inout): Pointer to an iterator structure provided by the caller. It must neither be modified nor released by the application during the entire iteration process (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00065">[SWS_KeyM_00065]</a>).
    </li>
    <li>
      <code>CertElementData</code> (out): Pointer to the buffer allocated by the caller, into which the element data is copied upon successful execution.
    </li>
    <li>
      <code>CertElementDataLength</code> (inout): Passes on the input side the maximum length of the data buffer. Upon return of <code>E_OK</code>, the value is overwritten with the actually written byte length (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00065">[SWS_KeyM_00065]</a>).
    </li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    The function returns the following status values via type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00065">[SWS_KeyM_00065]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: Element successfully found, data provided in the buffer, and iterator updated accordingly.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: Element data was not found. The iterator must no longer be used for any further calls.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The provided data buffer is too small for the certificate element.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: Invalid certificate ID or invalid certificate element ID.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_EMPTY</code>: No certificate data is available (certificate is empty).</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERT_INVALID</code>: The certificate is invalid or was not successfully verified.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    <code>KeyM_CertElementGetNext</code> operates synchronously and is reentrant for exactly one iterator (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00065">[SWS_KeyM_00065]</a>). Parallel calls must therefore not use the same iterator.
  </p>
  <p class="ai-note">
    This usage note is based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11 (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00065">[SWS_KeyM_00065]</a>).
  </p>
</div>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous interface <code>KeyM_CertGetStatus</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00066" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00066">[SWS_KeyM_00066]</a>) serves to query the current status of a certificate in the Key Manager (KeyM). The function is available via the header file <code>KeyM.h</code> and has the Service ID <code>0x12</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Input parameter:</strong> <code>CertId</code> (type <code>KeyM_CertificateIdType</code>) passes the identifier of the certificate concerned.</li>
<li><strong>Output parameter:</strong> <code>Status</code> (type <code>KeyM_CertificateStatusType*</code>) returns the determined state of the certificate.</li>
<li><strong>Return value (<code>Std_ReturnType</code>):</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The certificate status was successfully determined and provided.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: Providing the status is currently not possible.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4>Error handling</h4>
<p>In case of error, the function returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code>. If an invalid certificate ID is passed via <code>CertId</code>, the error <code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code> (&ldquo;Invalid certificate ID&rdquo;) is assigned (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00066" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00066">[SWS_KeyM_00066]</a>).</p>
<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>The function is specified as synchronous and non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00066" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00066">[SWS_KeyM_00066]</a>). Concurrent calls are not permitted without higher-level synchronization.</p>
<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification SWS_KeyM_00066.</p>
</div>

It is called immediately upon invocation of <code>KeyM_Start</code> if the configuration switches <code>KeyMCryptoKeyStartFinalizeFunctionEnabled</code> and <code>KeyMCryptoKeyHandlerStartFinalizeEnabled</code> are set to <code>TRUE</code>. Only when the function returns <code>E_OK</code> does the Key Manager transition into the active state, so that subsequent key updates are permitted.
  </p>
  <p>
    The passed parameters include (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00067" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00067">[SWS_KeyM_00067]</a>):
  </p>

    <li><code>RequestData</code> (in) and <code>RequestDataLength</code> (in): Additional data of the request (for example a signature) as well as the length of this data in the array.</li>
    <li><code>ResponseData</code> (out): Buffer for the response data to be returned by the function.</li>
    <li><code>ResponseDataLength</code> (inout): Passes upon call the maximum number of available bytes in <code>ResponseData</code> and returns upon <code>E_OK</code> the actual number of written bytes.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> provides specific status and error codes (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00067" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00067">[SWS_KeyM_00067]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The start operation was successfully executed; key update operations are now permitted.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The start operation was not accepted.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_PARAMETER_MISMATCH</code>: A parameter does not match the expected value.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_KEY_CERT_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The size of a parameter or buffer does not match.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    The function is specified as <em>Non Reentrant</em> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00067" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00067">[SWS_KeyM_00067]</a>). It is processed synchronously in the context of <code>KeyM_Start</code> and must not be called concurrently for overlapping key operations.
  </p>

<p>The parameters of the function are defined according to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00068" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00068">[SWS_KeyM_00068]</a>:</p>

<li><code>Request Data Length</code> (in): Length of the data in the passed request array.</li>
<li><code>Response Data Ptr</code> (out): Pointer to the buffer for the response data returned by the function.</li>
<li><code>Response Data Length</code> (inout): On the input side, the maximum number of bytes available in the response buffer; on the output side, the number of bytes actually returned.</li>

  </p>

    </li>
    <li>

    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Return value:</strong> Returns <code>Std_ReturnType</code>, where <code>E_OK</code> is defined as the return value (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00073" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00073">[SWS_KeyM_00073]</a>).

Since the specification lists only <code>E_OK</code> as the return value, the success or failure of the verification for the application is presumably transported exclusively via the parameter <code>Result</code> (interpretation). Specific error codes, DET, or DEM messages are not listed for this interface (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00073" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00073">[SWS_KeyM_00073]</a>).
  </p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="9bad93ada4f73e6fcb6801d539803818ae957c955bf283c45b156f5307cd96d4" data-trace-output="74627f75fc002194ea922c7e5d7ab2b4637372c85805994441abb5a21f3e1f63" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and purpose</h4>
  <p>
    The callback function <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00077" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00077">[SWS_KeyM_00077]</a> is called by the Key Manager to notify the higher-level application of the completion of a key update (<em>crypto key update operation</em>). It is specified as synchronous and reentrant, has no return value (<code>void</code>), and is declared via the header file <code>KeyM_Externals.h</code>.
  </p>

  <h4>Parameters</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>Result</code>: Contains the overall result of the update operation.</li>
    <li><code>ResultDataLength</code>: Indicates the length of the resulting result data of this operation, if present.</li>
    <li><code>ResultDataPtr</code>: Pointer to the generated result data.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Buffer Management</h4>
  <p>
    The buffer management and the notification sequence are strictly coupled to the update process:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00156" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00156">[SWS_KeyM_00156]</a>, the calling function of <code>KeyM_Update()</code> must pass a buffer pointer <code>ResultDataPtr</code>. Provided that <code>KeyM_Update()</code> accepts the operation with <code>E_OK</code>, this buffer must not be touched by the caller until the callback <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00077" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00077">[SWS_KeyM_00077]</a> has occurred. All results of <code>KeyM_Update()</code> are copied into this buffer, and the same pointer is passed back to the callback as <code>ResultDataPtr</code>.
    </li>
    <li>
      According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00093" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00093">[SWS_KeyM_00093]</a>, the notification <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00077" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00077">[SWS_KeyM_00077]</a> is triggered by the function <code>KeyM_Update()</code> as soon as the key handler returns and terminates the operation with <code>KEYM_KH_UPDATE_FINISH</code>. In doing so, the result data from <code>KeyM_KH_Update::ResultDataPtr</code> is transferred into the buffer provided by <code>KeyM_Update::ResultDataPtr</code>, and the return value of the key handler is used.
    </li>
  </ul>

  <p class="ai-note">
    This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.
  </p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="0c572fac430c2448b44246f29eaf842a874be787c619a5a99784bb8e4c06287a" data-trace-output="78ba16f416a9d3f63017c659649d9e31bc2ec1a11d7fa038f4a4da4b8620b7a4" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The notification function <code>KeyM_CryptoKeyFinalizeCallbackNotification</code> informs the application that a crypto key finalize operation (<em>crypto key finalize operation</em>) has terminated (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00079" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00079">[SWS_KeyM_00079]</a>). It is available via the header file <code>KeyM_Externals.h</code> and is typically provided by the application as a callback.</p>
  <p>The function returns no value (<code>void</code>) and processes the following input parameters (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00079" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00079">[SWS_KeyM_00079]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>Result</code> (<code>KeyM_ResultType</code>): Contains information about the outcome or result of the performed operation.</li>
    <li><code>ResultDataLength</code> (<code>uint16</code>): Indicates the length of the resulting data of this operation.</li>
    <li><code>ResultDataPtr</code> (<code>const uint8*</code>): Points to the result data in the buffer that had been passed to the original service function.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Execution Context and Configuration</h4>
  <p>According to the specification, the function is defined as synchronous and reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00079" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00079">[SWS_KeyM_00079]</a>). Accordingly, the application-side handler routine must be designed for multiple or concurrent calls.</p>
  <p>The provision and invocation of this callback are optional and bound to the pre-configuration: The callback function is only invoked and required if the configuration parameter <code>KeyMCryptoKeyStartFinalizeFunctionEnabled</code> is set to <code>TRUE</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00079" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00079">[SWS_KeyM_00079]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>The result of the key finalization is signaled directly to the application via the parameter <code>Result</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00079" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00079">[SWS_KeyM_00079]</a>). Specific DET or DEM error notifications are not defined for this notification function in the specification.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.</p>
</div>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00081" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00081">[SWS_KeyM_00081]</a>, the function <code>KeyM_CryptoKeyVerifyCallbackNotification</code> serves as a callback to notify the application of the completion of a cryptographic key verification operation. The call is initiated by the Key Manager (KeyM). This interface is declared in header <code>KeyM_Externals.h</code>.</p>
<p>Execution is synchronous (Synchronous). The function has no return value (<code>void</code>) and accepts the following input parameters:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Result</code> (type <code>KeyM_ResultType</code>): Transfers the result and status information about the outcome of the verification operation.</li>
<li><code>KeyId</code> (type <code>uint32</code>): Identifies the unique ID of the key for which the verification was performed.</li>
<li><code>Result Data Length</code> (type <code>uint16</code>): Specifies the length of the resulting data of this operation, provided result data is present.</li>
<li><code>Result Data Ptr</code> (type <code>const uint8*</code>): Pointer to the buffer containing the result data of the verification.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00081" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00081">[SWS_KeyM_00081]</a>, the callback function is specified as reentrant (Reentrant). The implementation on the application side must therefore ensure that parallel calls—for example, for different key IDs—are processed in a thread-safe manner.</p>
<h4>Error handling</h4>
<p>No specific error messages (such as DET or DEM) or return values are defined in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_00081" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_00081">[SWS_KeyM_00081]</a>. The functional result of the verification is communicated directly to the application via the parameter <code>Result</code>.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="dc730981e3e7bb58404ea1cd5c67ce0c60da3c4a83882fd32a07c0278e64c4b3" data-trace-output="3fa410673f735465e8271755c9f81d375c248bb52c407bdf043d41c78cc04c18" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The type <code>KeyM_CertificateStatusType</code> is defined as an enumeration and represents the result of certificate checks as well as the current processing status of a certificate in the Key Manager (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_91003">[SWS_KeyM_91003]</a>). The type is available via the header <code>Rte_KeyM_Type.h</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_91003">[SWS_KeyM_91003]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Status Values and Error Interpretation</h4>
  <p>The enumeration values reflect both regular processing states and specific verification errors (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_91003">[SWS_KeyM_91003]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>KEYM_CERTIFICATE_VALID</code> (<code>0x00</code>): Certificate successfully parsed and verified.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_CERTIFICATE_INVALID</code> (<code>0x01</code>): Certificate invalid (unspecified error).</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_PARSED</code> (<code>0x02</code>): Not parsed so far.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_CERTIFICATE_PARSED_NOT_VALIDATED</code> (<code>0x03</code>): Certificate parsed, but not yet validated.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_CERTIFICATE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code> (<code>0x04</code>): Certificate not set.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_VALIDITY_PERIOD_FAIL</code> (<code>0x05</code>): Validity period invalid.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_SIGNATURE_FAIL</code> (<code>0x06</code>): Signature check failed.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_CHAIN_OF_TRUST</code> (<code>0x07</code>): Chain of trust invalid.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_TYPE</code> (<code>0x08</code>): Invalid certificate type.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_FORMAT</code> (<code>0x09</code>): Invalid format.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_INVALID_CONTENT</code> (<code>0x0A</code>): Invalid content.</li>
    <li><code>KEYM_E_CERTIFICATE_REVOKED</code> (<code>0x0B</code>): Certificate check failed due to invalid scope or revocation.</li>
  </ul>

  <p>Callers typically evaluate the status to determine whether a certificate has already been checked (<code>0x02</code>, <code>0x03</code>), is ready for use (<code>0x00</code>), or due to which specific cause the verification was rejected (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_KeyM_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_KeyM_91003">[SWS_KeyM_91003]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification for R20-11.</p>
